title: Predict direct JAL targets in fetch
motivation:
The pipeline currently treats every JAL as an EX-stage redirect, discarding the
already fetched target instruction and paying a control bubble for direct calls
and unconditional jumps. A JAL target is encoded entirely in the fetched
instruction, so it can be predicted exactly without a BTB, history table, or
aliasing risk. The previous combined JAL and conditional-branch proposal failed
during implementation compilation, making a narrower predictor the best path to
retain useful control-flow speedup with much lower RTL and timing risk.

divide. Those back-end hold cycles are opportunities to fetch one or two

title: Registered lookahead loop predictor
motivation:
The one-entry loop predictor reduced CoreMark cycles by about four percent, but
every prior predictor placed a tag comparison or instruction decode directly on
the fetch-to-PC path and lost much more Fmax than it gained in IPC. The sequential
fetch stream exposes the next word address one cycle early, allowing a loop-entry
lookup to finish in a register before the candidate branch reaches fetch.

collapsed Fmax. That result shows useful instruction-stall overlap exists,
